title: Robichaux and white bands left out of the history of Louisiana music
summary: La Rocca says histories credit only Negro bands and ignore white bands, string bands, the Fourth of July and Bastille Day celebrations, German bands and French opera musicians, and he recalls working on the French opera stage.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did Robichaux's band and Huron's band have a hot tone? Would you say they had a jazz tone or a legitimate tone or what?

Well, I'd say they played the same, I think they recorded I have never heard their records but for enough people I've heard they didn't have jazz. Now I'm not quoting myself because what I heard, I heard the same music in white bands. They mention many bands but they don't mention Bowers, the Christians, the Detroit's band and the Cordy's band. They don't mention none of the white bands, all the Negroes as a culture Louisiana music. That's not right. Because the culture of Louisiana music, it was because of so many parades, so many affairs that was given. Let me start in the beginning, I told you about the string bands that I played in and let me tell you some of the places where I went. On July the 4th, they celebrated, that was American Day. July the 14th was Bastille Day, some places, Southern Park, sometimes other places that different great big places that did these affairs. That'll last sometimes two days. Then they had the Volksfest which was German. They had three, four bands that have a whole German band there and plenty of other bands that they don't mention. There's none of this stuff here that they have here. They had men like Sontagy played in the French opera, Pippa Tony. Some men that, these Negroes and I then, many modern men couldn't even touch. They were men that come from the conservatory that learned their music away from here. They had Germans. There's one old man here who used to play at a college restaurant, Shutton. Mr. Shutton, he used to bomb down the alley too. I used to go as a young boy.
You know, he didn't mention none of these men

but Negroes. But they don't tell you what they played. They say what they played. But they don't have no proof. No white men played music. In the French opera, they'll tell you the Italians didn't have nothing. Most of it was Italian opera and Italian singers. There had other plays there. You're going to ask me why? I worked on the French opera stage. As a boy, I attended two arc lights on there. And many of the ideas I got from them. Listen to the songs that they used to play. Like playing counter melody. Two songs line at one time.
